title: Modular monolith with four modules
rule: Code lives in app/Modules/{Customers,Catalog,Orders,Billing}. New features go into the module that owns the data; do not create new top-level app/ folders for domain code.
why: One deployable unit: several customers self-host on a single box. Module seams keep a later extraction possible without paying for distributed systems now.

title: Tenant isolation is enforced by the model layer
rule: Every tenant-owned table has a tenant_id foreign key, and every tenant-owned model uses App\Support\Tenancy\BelongsToTenant. Never bypass the scope (withoutGlobalScope, DB::table on tenant tables) in request code. Console commands and jobs must bind TenantContext explicitly.
why: All tenants share one database. The scope is fail-closed (throws without a tenant) so a missing scope is a loud error, not a silent data leak.

title: Monetary columns use decimal(12,2)
rule: Store money in decimal(12,2) columns with the 'decimal:2' cast.

title: Modules talk to each other only through Contracts
rule: A module may use another module only through that module's Contracts namespace (e.g. App\Modules\Customers\Contracts\CustomerDirectory). Do not import another module's Models or Internal classes, and do not query its tables (DB::table, joins, raw SQL, Eloquent relations to its models). If the contract lacks what you need, extend the contract inside the owning module.
why: In March an Orders report joined the customers table directly and broke when Customers split name into display_name (ADR-005). Contracts let a module change its schema without breaking its callers.

title: Schema changes are expand/contract
rule: A release may only add tables, or add columns that are nullable or have a default. Never rename, drop or change the type of an existing column in the same release that stops using it, and never edit a migration that has already shipped (add a new one). When replacing a column, keep writing the legacy column too (dual-write) until a later contract release removes it.
why: Self-hosted customers upgrade on their own schedule and roll back by redeploying the previous build against an already-migrated database. Mobile v2 clients and customer reporting still read legacy columns.

title: HTTP layer uses Resources and validation per module
rule: Responses go through a JsonResource in the module's Http/Resources; input is validated with a FormRequest or $request->validate().
why: Keeps response shapes stable and reviewable.

title: Route-model binding is tenant-scoped only because of middleware order
rule: Keep ResolveTenantFromHeader ahead of SubstituteBindings (bootstrap/app.php). New route groups must run inside the api group.
why: Found while debugging a cross-tenant 200 on GET /api/orders/{order}: bindings resolved before the tenant was set.

title: Repository layer over Eloquent
rule: Do not add repository interfaces around Eloquent inside a module. Cross-module access uses Contracts (ADR-004); inside a module, use Eloquent directly.
why: Tried in 2025; doubled the code for no testability gain.

title: Order totals are computed in OrderTotalsCalculator
rule: Any change to how an order total is computed (discounts, fees) belongs in App\Modules\Orders\Services\OrderTotalsCalculator.
why: Recorded after a pricing fix so totals logic stays in one place.

title: Money is integer kobo
rule: Store money as bigInteger kobo columns cast with App\Support\Money\MoneyCast. The API accepts and returns naira as 2-decimal strings; parse with Money::fromNaira and never use floats. products.price is a legacy decimal column pending migration: read it through ProductCatalog::unitPrice() and do not copy that pattern.
why: Float and decimal rounding produced kobo-level mismatches against payment-provider settlements.

title: Lower-case customer emails before saving
rule: Normalise customer emails to lower case before insert and before uniqueness checks.
why: Agent observed a duplicate customer that differed only by case. Not yet reviewed.

title: Order numbers are never reused; orders are never hard-deleted
rule: Never hard-delete an order or reuse its number. To remove an order from normal use, soft-delete or archive it so its number stays in the database.
why: Finance reconciles bank payments by order number. In March a hard-deleted order's number was issued again, and a customer's payment was matched to a stranger's order.
